newsitem.title: USA: C-Cube Microsystems falls after earnings warning.
newsitem.headline: C-Cube Microsystems falls after earnings warning.

text.p: The stock of C-Cube Microsystems Inc. plunged more than 20 percent Tuesday after the company said it will report lower-than-expected earnings for its fiscal second quarter.
C-Cube fell $5.25, or 21 percent, to $20.25 on the Nasdaq market, where it was among the most actively traded issues with more than 4 million shares traded.

The company, which reported net income of $15.4 million, or 41 cents a share for the first quarter, said Tuesday that it expected to post earnings per share of between 20 cents and 25 cents for the second quarter, which ends June 30.
C-Cube, which makes digital video devices, also said it expected second-quarter revenues of about $70 million to $75 million, well below the $94 million it pulled in during the first quarter.
It said the reduced sales were due to lower demand that reflects a seasonal slowdown and to continued price declines in response to competition.

The company, which is based in Milpitas, Calif., said most of its expected shortfall in revenue and earnings will come from reduced sales of its MPEG1 decoders used in video compact disc players sold in China.
